findings.markdown_says: ## Page 44 # ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E) --- **3.111** **internal data** all data described in a source unit except external data and external file connectors --- **3.112** **key of reference** key, either prime or alternate, currently being used to access records within an indexed file --- **3.113** ... (a `---` thematic break inserted after the running header and after EVERY ONE of the ten entries 3.111-3.120; eleven spurious rules in total on this page, at ISO_COBOL.md lines 1994, 2000, 2006, 2014, 2020, 2026, 2032, 2038, 2045, 2051, 2057)
findings.why_it_matters: `---` is the transcription's reserved page-break separator: elsewhere in ISO_COBOL.md it appears exactly once per page, immediately before the `` anchor. Page 44 emits eleven additional `---` rules INSIDE the page. No normative text is lost, but any consumer that segments the markdown on `---` (the reconciliation slicer, a chunker, a diff-by-page tool) will see eleven phantom page boundaries in the middle of clause 3 and mis-attribute entries 3.111-3.120 to eleven different 'pages'. The rules also render as horizontal lines that are not in the PDF.
findings.suggested_repair: Delete the eleven `---` lines between the running header and entry 3.120 on page 44 (ISO_COBOL.md lines 1994-2057), leaving only the single page-separator `---` that precedes the `` anchor. Match the blank-line-separated entry layout used on pages 38-43 and 45-48.
